14526163174.task: Write a Python module and save it as roman.py. It has two functions. 1) to_roman(n) returns the Roman numeral of an integer from 1 to 3999 as a string (to_roman(1994) is 'MCMXCIV'). 2) from_roman(s) returns the integer of a Roman numeral (from_roman('XLII') is 42). Test both yourself before you finish. Then tell me, each on its own line, the value of to_roman(954) and of from_roman('MMMCMXCVII').

14527107867.task: Write a Python module and save it as durations.py. It has two functions. 1) to_seconds(s) returns the seconds of a duration written with the units h, m and s, any of them left out (to_seconds('1h30m15s') is 5415, to_seconds('45m') is 2700). 2) to_text(n) writes a number of seconds that way, leaving out units that are zero (to_text(5415) is '1h30m15s', to_text(3600) is '1h', to_text(0) is '0s'). Test both yourself before you finish. Then tell me, each on its own line, the value of to_seconds('19h19m37s') and of to_text(0).
